# **Update on Contribution Amount for Act 4 and Act 800 in accordance with the Increment of the Wage Ceiling Limit**

Effective 1 October 2024, PERKESO will enforce a new wage ceiling for contributions from RM5,000 to **RM6,000** per month. The contribution amount that apply to employees with salaries exceeding RM5,000 per month is stated in the Third Schedule, Act 4 and the Second Schedule, Act 800. For employees with salaries exceeding RM6,000 per month, the contribution amount is subject to the wage ceiling of RM6,000.
Accordingly, the contribution payment for the month of October 2024 and the subsequent months shall be made by the employer according to the new wage ceiling.

The contribution rates for **Foreign Workers** are refer to the **Third Schedule (Act 4)** **,** whereas **Domestic Workers'** contribution rates are based on **eligibility** criteria listed in the **Domestic Worker** section.

**SOCIAL SECURITY ORGANISATION (PERKESO)**

**FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS (FAQ)**

**TEXT FILE FORMAT FOR EMPLOYEE CONTRIBUTIONS**

**1\.**

**What is the Employee Contribution Text File?**

The Employee Contribution Text File is a combined record of employee

contributions under Act 4 (SOCSO / PERKESO) and Act 800 (EIS) based on the

new format, which is required to be used by employers.

**2\.**

**What information is contained in the Employee Contribution Text File?**

The Employee Contribution Text File contains information such as employer code,

employee name, employee NRIC number, employee wages, as well as employer

and employee contribution shares, which are segregated according to the

respective Act and contribution month. Information on employer code, employee

name, employee NRIC number, and employee wages **are mandatory fields**

**3\.**

**Who is required to use this text file?**

This text file is for employers using the ASSIST 2.0 portal, which will be
implemented starting in June 2026 for the submission of contribution records. The

file must be uploaded through the portal.

**4\.**

**Can outstanding (arrears) contributions be submitted using this text file?**

Yes, arrears contributions can also be submitted using this text file.

2 | 11

**5\.**

**When can employers start using this new text file format?**

Employers may use this new text file format in the ASSIST 2.0 Portal.

**6\.**

**If employers wish to submit contribution records for only one Act, for**

**example Act 4 (SOCSO/PERKESO) only, Act 800 (EIS) only, or SKBBK only,**

**can this text file be used?**

Yes, this text file can be used to submit contribution records for a single Act only, if

there is no contribution deduction under the other Acts. For example, government

employers are only required to contribute under Act 4. For Acts with no deduction,

employers may either enter the amount as 0.00 or leave it blank.

**7\.**
**Can the previous single text file format based on individual Acts still**

**be used?**

Yes, the single text file format based on individual Acts may still be used until

30 September 2026. However, starting from 1 October 2026, all contribution

record submissions must use this new text file format.

**8\.**

**How is the SKBBK contribution amount entered in the single text file?**

SKBBK contribution amount must be calculated together with the existing

employer and employee shares for SOCSO / PERKESO contributions. PERKESO

system will then allocate the SKBBK amount based on the total contribution

entered in the text file.

**9\.**

**What is the employee contribution schedule for the LINDUNG 24 Jam**

**Scheme?**

The new contribution schedule, which incorporates the employee's share for the

LINDUNG 24 Jam Scheme, is scheduled to take effect on **1 June 2026** , as detailed

in Appendix 1.

3 | 11

**10\.**

**Who can be contacted for further enquiries?**
Enquiries may be directed to the PERKESO Customer Service Officer via email at

perkeso@perkeso.gov.my or by telephone at 1-300-22-8000.

results.title: Skim Kemalangan Bukan Bencana Kerja (LINDUNG 24 JAM) - English
excerpts:
“Non-employment injury” means a personal injury to the employee caused by accident not arising out of and in the course of his employment in an industry to which this Act applies and shall not include any circumstances specified in section 96B.

# Contribution Rate:

Contributions are fully borne by employees.
Employee contribution rates will be implemented in phases:

* 0\.75% for the first two years (Phase 1),
* 1\.0% for the next three years (Phase 2),
* 1\.25% from the sixth year onwards (Phase 3)

# Type of Contribution:

* It is **no longer compulsary** for **local employees** . Instead, participation is **voluntary** , and the contributions are **fully borne** by the **employees** . However, it remains **mandatory** for **foreign workers** in accordance with existing legal provisions.
* Employers shall pay contributions on behalf of employees for as long as the employee remains employed with them.

# Excluded Cases:

* Accidents happening outside the territory of Malaysia
* Insured Persons (OB) who are foreign workers that misuse valid passes or permits issued by the Director General of Immigration or violate any conditions of entry under the Immigration Act 1959 / 63 [Act 155].
* Self-employment injuries under Act 789.
* Domestic injuries under Act 838.
* Conditions caused by any illness such as diabetes, fever, high blood pressure, and others.

results.title: Levy Calculation Guideline - HRD Corp Support Centre
excerpts:
_ Example of wages **Exempted** from Levy Calculation:

\-Bonuses and commissions

\-Gratuity on discharge or retirements

\-Fund/scheme contribution to employee benefits or welfare.

\-Travel allowances including petrol and transport allowances

\-Apprenticeship

\-Special expenses

Example of non-fixed allowance **Exempted** from Levy Calculation:

\-Overtime payment

\-Night work allowance

\-Shift allowance

\-Attendance allowance (for which the amount changes from month-to=month)

\-Production incentive

\-Other similar types of allowances **Example : Current Levy**

Levy month = Salary month

01/2022 = January 2022

\-Payment before or on 15/2/2022, payment within 15 days of the following month;

\-Payment made after 15 days of the following month becomes levy in arrears due to exceeding the stipulated period.

**SAMPLE LEVY CALCULATION**

**​**

**LEVY = [(BASIC SALARY - UNPAID LEAVE) + FIXED ALLOWANCE] x 1%**
\*\*2 decimal place **Section 14 of the PSMB Act 2001** Every employer to whom this act applies shall be subject to human resources development levy at **1% of the monthly wage** of the employee. **Section 15 of the PSMB Act 2001** An employer with less than the required minimum number of employees, may opt to be registered in the class specified in Part II of the First Schedule, and shall pay a levy for each of his employee at the rate of **0\.5% of the monthly wages** of the employee. **Invalidity Scheme  
(LINDUNG PEKERJA)**

Protection for foreign workers who suffer from invalidity due to a permanent morbid condition which is either incurable or is not likely to be cured resulting to an inability to earn a living, through work corresponding to his strength and physical ability, equivalent to at least 1/3 of the customary earnings of a normal worker. This scheme covers invalidity or death of the foreign worker irrespective of the cause.

Effective date: **1 July 2024**

**Non-Employment Injury Scheme (LINDUNG 24 JAM)**

The Non-Employment Injury Scheme provides 24-hour protection to **foreign workers** against accidents that happen outside working hours and not related to the employment.

Effective date: **1 June 2026**

# **Eligibility Conditions for foreign workers:**

* Possess valid passport
* 'Possess valid work pass such as Visit Pass (Temporary Employment), employment pass, special pass and other related work passes.'
# **Registration and Contribution Payment**

Employers are responsible for registering their foreign workers and must ensure that the mandatory contributions are paid in full based on the specified contribution rates. Failure to do so is an offence under Employees’ Social Security Act 1969 (Act 4) and if convicted, can be fined a maximum of RM10,000.00 or 2 years imprisonment or both.

|MANDATORY monthly contribution payment : |Share |Employment Injury Scheme |Invalidity Scheme |Non Employment Accident Injury Scheme |Total Contribution |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|Employer |1\.25% |0\.5% |\- |1\.75% |
|Foreign Worker |\- |0\.5% |0\.75%  
(Phase 1) |1\.25% |

\* The contribution rate for the Non-Employment Injury Scheme is being implemented in three phases based on the year of implementation starting 1 June 2026:

* Years 1-2 (Phase 1) : 0.75%
* Years 3-5 (Phase 2) : 1.00%
* Years 6 onwards (Phase 3) : 1.25%

[Contribution Calculator](https://www.perkeso.gov.
my/en/our-services/protection/foreign-worker.html?view=article&id=969:kalkulator-caruman&catid=24 "Contribution Calculator")

# **Important Note**

**First Category Contribution (Employment Injury Scheme, Invalidity Scheme and Non-Employment Injury Scheme)  
** For foreign workers who first enter the PERKESO scheme or contribute for the first time before reaching the age of 55 years old.

**Second Category Contribution (Employment Injury Scheme and Non-Employment Injury Scheme)**  
For foreign workers who have reached the age of 55 years old when first entering the PERKESO scheme, or foreign workers who have reached the age of 60 years and are still working.

Please visit the following pages to learn more :

Registration

Contribution Rate

# **Benefits Offered**

**Employment Injury Scheme And Non-Employment Injury Scheme**

Medical Benefit

This benefit is in the form of free medical treatment at PERKESO’s panel clinic or government clinic/hospital.
